_note: THE SEVEN LINES A RIGHT-CLICK OFFERS on any PSK31 or Olivia row that names a station.
Ruled by Tim on 2026-09-21 (PHASE_PLAN.md R39, ruled C), written by work instruction 378.
WHAT A ROW IS. Each entry in "lines" has a "label", which is what the menu item reads,
and then EITHER a "macro" naming one of Hamlet's own three - answer, report, confirm -
OR a "text" carrying the words to send. A row may not have both, and a row with neither
is a row Hamlet cannot read.
WHAT GOES ON THE AIR. A "text" line is framed before it is sent: both callsigns in front
and the hand-back behind, exactly as a line you type on a card is framed -
W1AW de KC3QIS  <your line>  BTU W1AW de KC3QIS K. You write the middle; Hamlet writes
the rest. A "macro" line is the macro Hamlet already composes, unchanged.
WHAT IS SENT IS HELD TO THE SAME LIMIT AS EVERYTHING ELSE: thirty seconds of audio on
PSK31, and the same count of characters charged at the variant's own rate on Olivia. A
line that will not fit is refused before anything is keyed, in a sentence saying so.
PSK31 carries the Latin-1 set and nothing else, so a character outside it is dropped.
YOUR OWN COPY. Put a copy of this file at %AppData%\Hamlet\canned.json and Hamlet reads
that one instead of this one - the same folder settings.json and scan-segments.json live
in. Hamlet never writes either file, never creates your copy and never repairs it. If
your copy cannot be read, the menu says so and offers nothing rather than guessing.
